summary.title: Writing a Linux Debugger: Part 1 - Setup
summary.one_liner: You learn how to launch a child process under ptrace with fork/exec and build a minimal command loop with linenoise to halt and continue it.
takeaways: Launch a debuggee with fork() and execl(), with the child calling ptrace(PTRACE_TRACEME) first.
Use waitpid() in the parent to wait for the SIGTRAP sent when the traced process starts.
Build a simple REPL with linenoise for command input, history, and navigation.
Implement a continue command using PTRACE_CONT followed by waitpid().
Parse DWARF debug info with libelfin, which also provides a DWARF expression evaluator for reading variables.
summary.summary: This is the first part of a multi-part tutorial on writing a debugger for Linux programs, focused on C and C++. It explains the setup: using linenoise for command-line input and libelfin (preferred over libdwarf for its nicer interface and DWARF expression evaluator) for debug information. The main code walks through launching the target with the fork/exec pattern and ptrace, creating a debugger class with a run loop, and handling a simple continue command. The post is intentionally simplified, skipping robust error handling in favour of a working minimal debugger.
